name: South Sudan
tagline: The Sudd, and the second-largest migration on earth
summary: A million white-eared kob moving across Boma and Badingilo, the Sudd wetland the size of Belgium, and the cattle camps of the Mundari — the youngest country in the world, and the least travelled.
when: The dry season, December to March. Everything else is under water or unreachable.

entries.caption: Cattle Camps at Dawn
entries.description: Mundari herders and their Ankole cattle in smoke from dung fires, on the White Nile.
entries.subject: Mundari herders among long-horned cattle in dung smoke at dawn

entries.caption: The Sudd
entries.description: One of the largest wetlands on earth, where the Nile spreads out and slows almost to a stop.
entries.subject: papyrus and open water stretching to the horizon in the Sudd

entries.caption: The Great Kob Migration
entries.description: White-eared kob, tiang and Mongalla gazelle — counted at over a million animals.
entries.subject: a vast herd of white-eared kob crossing open grassland

entries.caption: Boma and Badingilo
entries.description: Two parks either side of the migration route, with almost no infrastructure and no crowds.
entries.subject: open grassland and scattered trees in Boma National Park

entries.caption: The Imatong
entries.description: Mount Kinyeti at 3,187 metres on the Ugandan border, the highest point in the country.
entries.subject: the forested slopes of the Imatong mountains rising to Mount Kinyeti

entries.caption: Fula Falls
entries.description: The Nile dropping through rock at Fula, on its way north out of Uganda.
entries.subject: white water at the Fula rapids on the White Nile

entries.caption: The White Nile
entries.description: It runs the length of the country and it is the reason for everything here.
entries.subject: a fishing canoe on the White Nile at sunset near Juba

entries.caption: No Coast, Plenty of Water
entries.description: Landlocked, but the river islands and sandbars near Terekeka do the job.
entries.subject: a sandbar and shallow water on the White Nile near Terekeka

entries.caption: The Southern Forests
entries.description: Guinea-Congolian rainforest at the Congo border, with forest elephant and chimpanzee in it.
entries.subject: dense rainforest canopy in the Western Equatoria forest belt

entries.caption: Getting to Boma
entries.description: Light aircraft and then hours of track. It is expedition travel and it is honest about that.
entries.subject: a light aircraft on a grass airstrip in remote grassland

entries.caption: Sixty-Four Peoples
entries.description: Dinka, Nuer, Shilluk, Bari, Azande, Mundari and fifty-eight more, in a country of twelve million.
entries.subject: a group of young men at a Mundari cattle camp in the evening

entries.caption: The Mundari
entries.description: Cattle are wealth, name and argument. A camp of them at dusk is unlike anything else.
entries.subject: a Mundari man resting against the flank of a long-horned bull

entries.caption: Kisra, Asida and Fish
entries.description: Sorghum asida, kisra flatbread, and Nile perch grilled on the bank.
entries.subject: grilled Nile perch and flatbread served on a riverbank

entries.caption: Wrestling
entries.description: Dinka and Mundari wrestling matches draw whole districts, with drumming and singing round the ring.
entries.subject: traditional wrestlers and a drumming crowd at a village match

entries.caption: Beadwork and Corsets
entries.description: Dinka beaded corsets in colours that state a man's age set, and Azande basketry.
entries.subject: a beaded Dinka corset in red and blue on display

entries.caption: Lado and the Old Posts
entries.description: The Lado Enclave, Gondokoro and the river stations of the nineteenth-century Nile expeditions.
entries.subject: the ruins of a colonial-era river station on the White Nile

entries.caption: Nothing on the List Yet
entries.description: No World Heritage sites, and a heritage that is living rather than ruined.
entries.subject: elders sitting under a large tree at a village meeting

entries.caption: Juba
entries.description: A river port that became a capital in 2011 and has been building ever since.
entries.subject: the riverfront and low buildings of Juba on the White Nile

entries.caption: Tukuls
entries.description: Round mud walls, conical thatch, and a shape that has not needed improving.
entries.subject: a cluster of thatched tukul houses in a South Sudanese village

entries.caption: Market Day at Terekeka
entries.description: Cattle, sorghum, fish and tea, and the whole district in one place.
entries.subject: a busy open-air market with cattle and traders at Terekeka

entries.caption: Hard Country for It
entries.description: This is not a family destination yet, and pretending otherwise would not help anyone.
entries.subject: a village school class sitting outside under a tree

entries.caption: Walking the Imatong
entries.description: Cool forest, waterfalls and Kinyeti, from Gilo. Guides are essential and available.
entries.subject: a forest path climbing through the Imatong mountains

entries.caption: Two Camps
entries.description: There is a mobile camp on the migration and very little else. That is the honest position.
entries.subject: a mobile tented camp pitched on open grassland

entries.caption: The Sudd Holds the Nile Back
entries.description: Half the water entering the Sudd evaporates in it. The wetland is a climate system.
entries.subject: papyrus swamp and open channels in the Sudd wetland from the air

entries.caption: Smoke and Horns
entries.description: A Mundari camp at first light, when the fires are lit and the light comes through them.
entries.subject: sunlight through dung smoke over cattle horns at a Mundari camp

entries.caption: Nimule
entries.description: A small park on the Ugandan border with elephant, and the Nile going through it.
entries.subject: the Nile running through green hills at Nimule

entries.caption: Why South Sudan
entries.description: A migration to rival the Serengeti's, seen by a few dozen people a year.
entries.subject: a single vehicle beside an immense herd of kob on open plain
